posts.author: enerjakRBY
posts.body:
Trying to do this with common events and no plugins, is there a way to have 2 separate characters function as 1 unit? So like as an example, not actually in my game, you have a character like Mario, and another like Luigi, but instead of taking two slots on the battlefield, they take one, and after each of their actions they switch to the other brother. So like the party would be:
"Bowser"
"Peach"
"Mario/Luigi"
Untargetable Npc: rescue character (for if the other characters fall in battle, they rescue the party by taking them to the last safe area. Trying to do this all without plugins, and found this to be the best outcome to prevent game over)

posts.author: ShadowDragon
posts.body:
if Mario/Luigi is selectable who to pick,  you can exclude it.
or save that one to a variable.
or add them to a variable as array, than pick out the actor ID
to be in battle, keep the other in the array.
so if swapping, you can swap the actor ID from mario to luigi.
but it really depends how you event this and how the gameplay works.

posts.author: enerjakRBY
posts.body: Would both characters be able to act on the same turn using this, or would they need to alternate turns, so long as the other of the pair is not ko'd (1. M, 2. L, etc)

posts.author: DevRPG2k
posts.body:
enerjakRBY said:
and after each of their actions they switch to the other brother
Click to expand...
You will need to create unique skills for these two characters. Remember that the "0001: Attack" skill is used by all monsters and actors; they will also need a skill that simulates a regular attack.
Remember that both will need to have battle graphics that simulate the interaction between them:

posts.author: DevRPG2k
posts.body:
I'm sorry, I misinterpreted what you needed. I was only thinking about the mechanics of the Mario & Luigi RPG and ended up misunderstanding.
If you modify the common event to not switch members and only add different forced actions while still using the unique skills method, I believe you'll get very close to the result.
